prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the one shortlisted candidate that the opening ballots converge on: four members place it in their top three and eight of eight rank it, which is the broadest support on the list. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted a flat band at a specific twist angle in 2011, and the 2018 Cao et al. experiments from Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle, so the prediction and the discovery are a tight, falsifiable theory-plus-experiment pair. Independent groups have reproduced the phases, and the idea has spread to a large family of moire systems with tunable interactions and topology. After reading colleagues' arguments I now put it ahead of my own opening first choice, circuit QED (B014), for reasons of timing and independence of judgement explained below.
statement.case_against: The interpretation of the superconductivity is still contested, and the field is young, so the committee may reasonably say the central physical question is not yet settled and that the discovery is early relative to the maturity of B022, B037 or B031. The experimental credit is also not clean: Cao and co-workers did the decisive measurements and other groups (Dean and others on related moire systems) extended them, so three names necessarily simplify a collaborative result.

responses.point: Ranks B028 second and stresses that theory (Bistritzer and MacDonald) paired with Jarillo-Herrero's experiment is a clean pairing, while noting the credit is not entirely clean because of the Cao et al. team and reproduction by others.
responses.response: I agree that the pairing is the strongest argument for B028 and share the attribution concern about the larger team. I disagree slightly that it is a weakness of this candidate in particular: Nobel credit to a group leader for a first-author-driven discovery is standard practice, and the theory prediction predates the experiment by seven years and named the magic angle. I am more cautious than you about the superconductivity, since mechanism is unresolved, but the prize would honour the flat-band prediction and the correlated-phase discovery, not a pairing theory.

responses.point: Ranks B003 (cavity method and message passing) first and B028 second, valuing conceptual cleanness, and notes that B028 interpretation is mature phenomenologically but not fully settled.
responses.response: I take your point that the pairing mechanism is open, and I would resist citing superconductivity as the achievement. I would note, though, that your first choice rests on methods whose origin lies substantially with Parisi, who is already a laureate, so the attribution problem for B003 is arguably sharper than for B028. I read the open mechanism as a reason to word the citation around flat bands and correlated phases, not as a reason to defer.

responses.point: Puts optical lattice clocks (B022) first, arguing for the Katori-Ye pairing as a clean, mature and measurement-driven advance with applications to fundamental constants and redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree that B022 is among the cleanest cases on attribution and maturity on the list, and clocks are plainly in the tradition of prizes for measurement. My reservation is limited: I rank it as an alternative rather than the preferred prize because I judge the conceptual reach of moire quantum matter to be broader, and the second's redefinition is still pending. I would not object strongly if the committee preferred B022; a two-person prize is easier to defend than the three-name B028.

responses.point: Leads with IceCube (B002) as an instrument-enabled discovery with confirmed diffuse flux, and prefers a narrower B031 credit (Kane and Molenkamp) to avoid mixing sub-results.
responses.response: I share your attraction to instrument-driven discovery, but I find the single-name credit for a collaboration-scale discovery a real weakness and would want the committee to discuss it before ranking B002 above B028. On B031 I agree that trimming to Kane and Molenkamp is cleaner, but it leaves out Mele and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that the HgTe experiment followed, and the credited-name list does not let us repair that.

responses.point: Places the Higgs discovery through ATLAS and CMS (B037) first, arguing it is fully mature and completes the experimental basis of the electroweak sector, with the theory already honoured.
responses.response: The science of B037 is first rank and I do not dispute maturity. My serious qualification is attribution: honouring conception and construction by Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee over the 2012 analysis leadership, and over thousands of collaborators, is a principle the committee would have to argue explicitly, and the supplied names depend on a contested reading. I would support it if the committee accepts that principle, but I do not think it clearly dominates B028.

uncertainties: Whether the experimental credit for B028 should include the first-author team (for example Yuan Cao) or other moire groups, which the three credited names cannot express.
Whether recognition of B028 is premature given the unsettled origin of the superconductivity.
Whether a prize for circuit QED (B014) is too close to the 2025 award for superconducting-circuit quantum effects, and whether omitting Girvin from a three-name B014 configuration is defensible.
Whether the committee will accept detector-conception credit for B037.
statement.conflict_note: Possible recusal issue on B014 and any other superconducting-circuit candidate: my research field is circuit and waveguide QED, I direct WACQT at Chalmers, and Chalmers colleagues (Delsing, Wilson) and frequent collaborators work in this area; Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. This is why I moved my preferred configuration away from my own opening first choice. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B028, B022 or the other shortlisted candidates.
